claim: Bar Néstor in Parte Vieja is famed for txuleta steak and a legendary potato tortilla, of which only two are made daily (one for lunch, one for dinner), requiring arrival at 11:30am or 6:30pm to sign the list.
quote: only two are made each day (one for lunch and one for dinner). In 2026, you still have to arrive at 11:30 AM or 6:30 PM just to get your name on the list for a single slice

claim: Borda Berri's signature pintxos include slow-cooked beef cheek, kokotxas de bacalao pil pil, and a creamy orzo risotto with Idiazábal cheese, with everything cooked to order.
quote: Beef cheek, slow-cooked until it practically dissolves, is one of the signature dishes, and the orzo with cuttlefish ink ... Creamy orzo risotto made with nutty idiazábal cheese

claim: La Cuchara de San Telmo, tucked off Calle 31 de Agosto, is famous for foie gras with apple and crisp-skinned cochinillo asado from a tiny seasonal blackboard menu; same owners as Borda Berri.
quote: The foie gras with apple is the pintxo they're famous for ... the cochinillo asado has skin so crisp you can hear it crack from across the room

claim: Ganbara is the Parte Vieja go-to for seasonal wild mushrooms — the revuelto de hongos (mushrooms with fried egg) and surtido de setas — and is reportedly Chef Juan Mari Arzak's favourite pintxos bar.
quote: Ganbara is known for its mushroom dishes, including the revuelto hongos (grilled mushrooms with a fried egg) and surtido setas (medley of wild mushrooms). It is Chef Arzak's favorite pintxos bar

claim: La Viña's Basque burnt cheesecake is the bar's signature, made from cream cheese, eggs, cream, sugar and a touch of flour, with a light creamy interior and caramelised crust.
quote: A classic Basque burnt cheesecake contains nothing more than cream cheese, eggs, cream, sugar and a bit of flour

claim: Bar Txepetxa serves anchovy fillets on toasted baguette with more than a dozen rotating toppings (spider crab cream, blueberry sauce, pepper-onion jardinera) and has been family-run for three generations.
quote: Every anchovy pintxo starts with two glimmering fillets on a warm toasted baguette slice, but from there there are more than a dozen toppings and condiments on offer, from spider crab cream to blueberry sauce to crunchy pepper-and-onion jardinera

claim: Bar Sport in Parte Vieja is renowned for its seared foie with pepper and sea urchin cream pintxo.
quote: The bar's most renowned pintxos include the seared foie with pepper and the sea urchin cream

claim: Goiz Argi's house specialty is grilled shrimp skewers (brochetas de gambas), and it also serves bacon-wrapped mushrooms.
quote: house specialty of grilled shrimp skewers was excellent. They also serve mushrooms wrapped in bacon

claim: Bar Zeruko is known for theatrical, creative pintxos, most famously 'la hoguera' — raw cod served on a smoking hot coal at the table.
quote: they are famous for their "la hoguera"—raw cod served over hot coals

claim: Bar Bergara in Gros, run by third-generation host Monti since the 1950s, is award-winning for innovative pintxos including 'Txalupa', 'Udaberri' and 'Itxaso', spanning beef in red wine, wild mushroom mini-risotto and seafood stew spoonfuls.
quote: With a long line of awards for its renowned "pinchos" ("Txalupa", "Udaberri", "Itxaso"), it carries on innovating and offering new "pinchos" to its clients

claim: Bergara's signature 'Txalupa' is a crunchy puff-pastry boat filled with mushrooms, cava and cream; in Gros, Bar Zabaleta is known for a tortilla pintxo selling over 100 a day and Hidalgo 56 for the 'volcán de morcilla' blood-sausage pintxo topped with egg yolk.
quote: Txulapa pintxo: "crunchy piece of puff pastry filled with mushrooms, cava, and cream" ... Tortilla pintxo: "Perfectly cooked with bits of onion and bell pepper, they sell over 100 a day" ... Volcán de morcilla: blood sausage volcano topped with egg yolk

claim: The official San Sebastián tourism board states that cold pintxos may be self-served from the bar top while hot pintxos must be ordered at the counter, payment is settled when leaving, and groups typically rotate rounds or use a shared kitty rather than paying individually.
quote: You generally pay when you are about to leave ... people here never pay for their own consumption in each bar

claim: Txikiteo (also called poteo) is the Basque ritual of moving from bar to bar, with the rule of thumb being one or two pintxos plus a small drink (zurito beer or txikito wine) per stop before moving on.
quote: the essence of txikiteo is movement—have one or two pintxos, pay, and move on to the next bar

claim: Pintxo-bar peak hours are roughly 1–3pm for lunch and 8–11pm for evening txikiteo, with most bars closing between 4:30pm and 7:30pm and many shuttered on Mondays.
quote: Most eateries will be closed between 4:30 PM and 7:00-7:30 PM ... Most are closed on Mondays

claim: La Cuchara de San Telmo and Borda Berri are the two most consistently recommended Parte Vieja pintxos bars by food press and online consensus, with La Cuchara known for creative à-la-minute hot pintxos and Borda Berri for modern Basque interpretations with premium ingredients.
quote: La Cuchara de San Telmo and Borda Berri are the most consistently recommended pintxos bars in San Sebastián. La Cuchara is known for creative hot pintxos served à la minute, while Borda Berri excels in modern interpretations

claim: La Concha bay is sheltered by Santa Clara island, producing unusually calm water; Ondarreta sits at the western end of the bay below Monte Igueldo with Miramar Palace separating it from La Concha.
quote: Ondarreta Beach is shielded by Monte Igeldo and at the foot of Miramar Palace, at the heart of La Concha Bay.

claim: Eduardo Chillida's Peine del Viento sits at the western end of Ondarreta beach: three 10-ton steel sculptures embedded in rocks at the foot of Monte Igueldo, designed with architect Luis Peña Ganchegui and installed in 1976.
quote: The Comb of the Wind is a collection of three sculptures by Eduardo Chillida arranged as an architectural work by the Basque architect Luis Peña Ganchegui... three of Chillida's monumental steel sculptures, weighing 10 tons each, embedded in natural rocks.

claim: Monte Igueldo funicular round-trip costs €5.50 adults / €2.50 children, one-way €4.00/€1.50; access to the viewpoint enclosure is an additional €3.00 per person.
quote: Round-trip: Adults €5.50 / Children (up to 7) €2.50. One-way: Adults €4.00 / Children €1.50. Enclosure/Lookout Access €3.00 per person.

claim: The Monte Igueldo funicular runs roughly 10am–9/10pm, departing every 15 minutes, and the summit hosts a vintage early-20th-century amusement park where rides are paid individually rather than via gate admission.
quote: The funicular is generally open every day from 10 a.m. to 9 or 10 p.m. and departs every 15 minutes... There is no admission fee for the amusement park, but rather a charge for each individual ride.

claim: Monte Urgull is free, open 08:00–21:00 May–September and 08:00–19:30 October–April, with night access closed.
quote: Access to Monte Urgull is closed at night. Opening times from 1 May to 30 September are 08:00-21:00; and opening times from 1 October to 30 April are 08:00-19:30.

claim: The Monte Urgull walk from sea level to Castillo de la Mota at the summit is under 1 km and takes about 30 minutes, though interconnected trails can absorb a couple of hours.
quote: The distance is less than a mile (about 1km) from sea level to castle, and the hike takes about 30 minutes to reach the castle, though trekkers can easily spend a couple of hours exploring the interconnected walking trails.

claim: The Sagrado Corazón statue crowning Monte Urgull is over 12 m tall (24 m including its base/chapel) and has stood since 1950; the Castillo de la Mota dates to the 12th century and houses a small free history museum.
quote: The Sagrado Corazón ("Sacred Heart") statue, measuring over 12 metres in height, has blessed the city since 1950 from the highest point of Monte Urgull, and rests upon a base which houses a chapel.

claim: The Paseo Nuevo is a 1.3 km promenade looping around the seaward base of Monte Urgull from the Old Town/Kursaal area; its vibe shifts from lively to calm as you walk away from the centre.
quote: The Paseo Nuevo is a wonderful promenade that surrounds Urgull mount... Along its 1.3 km stretch, the vibe gradually changes—from lively seaside to complete calm as you move away from the center.

claim: Paseo Nuevo is famous for wave-spotting near the Oteiza sculpture, where storm waves over 10 m can crash over the railing; police occasionally close the promenade in rough weather (mostly autumn/winter).
quote: The best known and most photographed zone for wave-spotting is the Paseo Nuevo alongside the sculpture by Oteiza, where waves of over 10 metres in height crash against the walls and leap into the air.

claim: Zurriola, in the Gros district between the Kursaal and Monte Ulía, stretches 800 m and is the city's surf hub with consistent waves drawing surfers year-round.
quote: Located in the district of Gros, between the Kursaal and Monte Ulía, the Zurriola Beach has become a favourite with surfers and youngsters who come from all over the world... 800 metres of sand occupied by the Zurriola.

claim: Zurriola/Playa de Gros works at all tides but is most consistent on a mid-incoming tide, with the biggest swells in autumn/winter; late spring is generally smaller and friendlier for lessons.
quote: Zurriola Playa de Gros

claim: Late-May weather in Donostia is mild but damp: highs near 18°C/64°F, lows around 12°C/54°F, ~17 rain days and ~116 mm precipitation across the month.
quote: In May, San Sebastián sees pleasant temperatures, with highs around 18°C (64°F) and overnight lows of 12°C (54°F)... Rainfall is fairly high at around 116 mm (4.6 in) on average, with roughly 17 days seeing rain.

claim: Ondarreta is the quietest of the three city beaches, measures roughly 500 m by 100 m of golden sand and has a playground on the sand, making it the family-friendliest option.
quote: Ondarreta is the least famous of the three city beaches and for the same reason it is also the quietest beach during the high season, making the beach perfect for those with children... There is a playground on the sand itself.

claim: The E20 Lurraldebus line connects Hondarribia with Errenteria, Pasai Antxo and Donostia/San Sebastián.
quote: Línea E20 - Hondarribia > Errenteria > Pasai Antxo > Donostia

claim: The E21 Lurraldebus line links San Sebastián airport with Hondarribia and Donostia city center (Plaza Gipuzkoa).
quote: Línea E21 (Invierno) - Aeropuerto San Sebastián > Hondarribia > Donostia

claim: The E21 bus operates daily roughly 06:55 to 21:45 with stops between Hondarribia airport and Plaza Gipuzkoa in San Sebastián.
quote: The E21 bus route operates every day with regular schedule hours from 06:55 to 21:45

claim: Hondarribia's Calle San Pedro is a pedestrian street of brightly painted fishers' houses with green or blue facades and flower-decked wooden balconies, lined with bars and restaurants.
quote: Calle San Pedro is a quaint pedestrian-only strip flanked by traditional fishers' houses, with facades painted bright green or blue, and wooden balconies cheerfully decorated with flower boxes.

claim: Hondarribia's old-town Plaza de Armas is dominated by the Castle of Charles V, now a Parador hotel.
quote: The highlight of the Plaza de Armas is a magnificent building called Castle of Charles V which now functions as a Parador Hotel.

claim: Getaria is roughly a 32-minute drive from San Sebastián, sitting between the sea and vine-covered mountains.
quote: Getaria is a short drive from San Sebastián, sitting sleepily on the coast between the sea and vine-covered mountains... San Sebastián is 32 minutes away.

claim: A Getaria day combines the Balenciaga Museum, lunch at one-Michelin-star Elkano (grilled whole fish), and txakoli vineyard visits.
quote: Balenciaga, Elkano and txakoli, discover Getaria

claim: The Cristóbal Balenciaga Museum in Getaria charges €14 general admission and €9 reduced; under-18s enter free. March–October hours are Tue–Sun 10:30–19:00, with July–August daily 10:30–20:00.
quote: General admission price is 14€... Reduced admission of 9€... March – October: Tuesday to Sunday from 10:30 – 19:00... July – August: Every day from 10:30 – 20:00

claim: The cliff walk from San Sebastián's Zurriola/Gros along the Monte Ulía range descends to the Faro de la Plata lighthouse before reaching Pasai San Pedro.
quote: the walk starts from Zurriola beach of Gros, goes along Ulía to the Faro de La Plata (silver lighthouse) and from there descends to Pasai San Pedro to cross later in the boat to Casa Cámara

claim: The Pasaia bay motora ferry between Pasai Donibane and Pasai San Pedro costs €1.10 one-way and runs roughly 6:30am–11:00pm (later on weekends).
quote: The single ticket costs 1.10€ with children under 3 traveling for free.

claim: Pasai Donibane is the picturesque side of Pasaia, with cobbled streets, colorful waterfront facades and landmarks including the Church of San Juan Bautista and Victor Hugo's house.
quote: Pasai Donibane is the most picturesque district, with its narrow cobbled streets, colorful facades, and waterfront promenade, highlighted by landmarks such as the Church of San Juan Bautista and Victor Hugo's House

claim: Pesa coaches between Bilbao and San Sebastián run hourly on Saturdays and take about 1h15.
quote: PESA operates every 60 minutes on Saturdays, with a journey time of 1hr 15 minutes

claim: The Euskotren regional train between San Sebastián and Bilbao takes about 2h40 (vs ~1h15 by bus), making the bus the practical option for a day trip.
quote: Train duration is approximately 2 hours 40 minutes (Euskotren) or 4 hours 30 minutes (Renfe), with Euskotren running every hour

claim: Adult admission to the Guggenheim Bilbao is €15 (€7.50 reduced, free under 18); Tuesday evenings 18:00–20:00 are free.
quote: Adult admission is €15, with a reduced rate of €7.50 for students and retired seniors, free entry for everyone under 18, and a free Tuesday evening window.

claim: The Guggenheim Bilbao was designed by Frank Gehry on the bank of the Nervión, with intentionally random-looking curves designed to catch the light.
quote: The building was designed by Canadian-American architect Frank Gehry and was built alongside the Nervion River. The curves on the exterior of the building were intended to appear random; the architect said that the randomness of the curves are designed to catch the light

claim: The Euskotren 'Topo' shuttle links San Sebastián with Hendaye (19 km, 35 min) every half hour, costing €2.90 one-way and €5.80 return.
quote: The rail shuttle linking Hendaye to San Sebastian takes just 35 minutes every day. Departures are every 3′ and 33′ of each hour... Hendaye/Donostia fare: €2.90, return fare: €5.80.

claim: A €14.30 two-day Euskotren pass covers unlimited travel on the San Sebastián–Irun–Hendaye line plus French TER services from Hendaye to Saint-Jean-de-Luz, Biarritz and Bayonne.
quote: €14.30 buys a 2-day pass giving unlimited travel on Euskotren San Sebastian-Irun-Hendaye and on French trains Hendaye-St Jean de Luz - Biarritz - Bayonne

claim: A seasonal maritime shuttle crosses the Bidasoa between Hondarribia and Hendaye in about 7 minutes for roughly €2–€2.60 cash, with bikes €0.50.
quote: There are 2 different companies operating this route: the Rekalde boat based in Hondarribia and the Marie Louise boat based in Hendaye... The crossing takes 7 minutes... Special rates for bicycles are €0.50

claim: Biarritz day-trip highlights include the Hôtel du Palais, the Phare de Biarritz lighthouse and the footbridge to the Rocher de la Vierge.
quote: you can admire the lavish beachfront Hôtel du Palais, visit the majestic Phare de Biarritz lighthouse, and walk the footbridge to the Rock of the Virgin Mary

claim: Biarritz's Aquarium / Musée de la Mer sits in front of the Rocher de la Vierge with 60+ tanks and daily seal feedings at 10:30 and 17:00.
quote: More than sixty aquariums await visitors to explore the richness of the seabed... daily seal feeding on the panoramic terrace, occurring at 10:30 am and 5 pm every day.

claim: In Saint-Jean-de-Luz, the Maison Louis XIV (built 1643) hosted the king for 40 days in 1660 around his marriage to the Spanish Infanta and is open to visitors April–November.
quote: Built in 1643 by a rich ship-owner, this house welcomed the young King Louis XIV for several months in 1660... Opening : from 04, April to 01, November 2026

claim: Saint-Jean-de-Luz's harbour, Church of Saint Jean Baptiste (site of the royal wedding with its baroque altarpiece) and the Infanta's house Joanoenia anchor a walkable historic centre.
quote: The Church of St John the Baptist was where the marriage of Louis XIV with the Infanta Maria Theresa of Spain was celebrated... A Historical Monument, the building boasts an exceptional décor and contains a monumental baroque altarpiece

claim: San Telmo Museoa charges €10 general admission, €4 reduced, closed Mondays (except holidays), free every Tuesday and on 18 May; winter hours Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00, summer 10:00-20:00.
quote: Open Tuesday-Sunday: Winter (Nov 1–Mar 31) 10am-7pm; Summer (Apr 1–Oct 31) 10am-8pm. Closed Mondays (except bank holidays). General admission 10,00 €. Reduced 4,00 €. Free Every Tuesday and on May 18th.

claim: San Telmo is housed in a 16th-century Dominican convent at the foot of Monte Urgull and presents Basque history, ethnography, society and culture.
quote: Museo San Telmo in San Sebastián — the oldest museum in the Basque Country, housed in a 16th-century Dominican convent.

claim: Aquarium Donostia tickets are €14 adults, €7 children 4-12, €10 reduced (seniors, students, unemployed), free under 4, and €3 extra for audio-tour.
quote: Adults: €14. Children (ages 4-12): €7. Seniors, Disabled Visitors, Students, Unemployed: €10. Under 4 years old: Free. Audio-Tour Service: €3 additional.

claim: Aquarium opens daily 10:00-20:00 in summer (Jul-Aug) and on weekends/holidays year-round; closed 25 Dec, 1 Jan and 20 Jan; closed Mondays outside Apr-Sept except long weekends.
quote: January, February, March, October-December: Tuesday-Friday 10:00-19:00; weekends/holidays 10:00-20:00. July-August: Daily 10:00-20:00. Closed Dec 25, Jan 1, Jan 20. Mondays closed outside April-September.

claim: Tabakalera, in San Sebastián's Egia district, occupies a former tobacco factory and houses contemporary art exhibitions, cinema, medialab, conference spaces and a café, with most areas free to enter.
quote: Contemporary art exhibitions, Cinema and audiovisual programming, Medialab (Creation library and laboratory), Conference and gathering spaces, Café (MODU). Free entrance for certain events.

claim: Tabakalera's fifth-floor rooftop terrace offers free panoramic views over the Urumea river and Gros, accessed via glass elevator, and the centre is a useful rainy-day refuge.
quote: Rooftop Terrace: Accessible via escalators or glass elevator. Offers views of the Urumea and Gros — perfect for a quick photo stop. Free entry to most areas.

claim: The Kursaal, designed by Rafael Moneo as 'Two Stranded Rocks' and opened 23 August 1999 beside Zurriola beach at the Urumea mouth, won the 2001 European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture (Mies van der Rohe).
quote: The building opened on August 23, 1999... In 2001, the Kursaal and Moneo received the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture. Two large prismatic volumes... double translucent glass panels.

claim: Moneo conceived the Kursaal's two translucent glass cubes as 'two giant beached rocks' nodding to Mounts Urgull and Ulia, exploring glass as a structural material for the first time.
quote: The two cubes are abstract volumes able to absorb and contain the program while becoming part of the landscape, nodding at Mount Urgull and Mount Ulia: the cubes, two giant beached rocks that honor the geography.

claim: Chillida-Leku in Hernani charges €14 adults, €10 reduced, free for children 0-7, and opens Thursday-Monday 10:00-18:00 (closed Tuesday-Wednesday).
quote: Entry Ticket: from €14.00. Adults €14, Reduced €10, Children (0-7 years) Free. Thursday–Monday: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Tuesday–Wednesday: Closed.

claim: Chillida-Leku reopened on 17 April 2019 after a partnership with Hauser & Wirth, adding the Pilar Belzunce room, restaurant, museum-grade lighting and improved accessibility to the 11-hectare park with ~40 sculptures around the 16th-century caserío Zabalaga.
quote: Chillida Leku reopened its doors to the public on Wednesday 17 April 2019. The sculpture park of 11 hectares featuring around 40 of the artist's works. Added the Pilar Belzunce room, a restaurant and café.

claim: Chillida-Leku is at Barrio Jauregui 66, 20120 Hernani, on the outskirts of Hernani near San Sebastián, reachable by bus BU05 from Donostia every half hour.
quote: Barrio Jauregui 66, 20120 Hernani, Gipuzkoa — situated on the outskirts of Hernani near San Sebastián.

claim: Catedral del Buen Pastor, opened 1897 by Manuel Echave in Neo-Gothic style modelled on Cologne and Ulm, has a 75 m spire and Spain's largest pipe organ (1954); admission is free, open Mon-Fri 08:30-12:30 and 17:00-20:00.
quote: Built by architect Manuel Echave and opened in 1897... towering spire reaches an impressive height of 75 meters... organ inaugurated in 1954 is the largest in Spain. Admission is free. Monday to Friday: 8:30am-12:30pm and 5:00pm-8:00pm.

claim: Basílica de Santa María del Coro in Parte Vieja is a Baroque church built 1743-1774 with a Churrigueresque façade topped by Saint Sebastian, sited at the foot of Monte Urgull at Calle 31 de Agosto and Calle Mayor.
quote: Baroque-style church completed in 1774 and located at the intersection of Calle 31 de Agosto and Calle Mayor in the Parte Vieja. Built between 1743 and 1774. Baroque façade with Churrigueresque touches topped by a sculpture of Saint Sebastian the Martyr.

claim: The Kursaal hosts the San Sebastián International Film Festival, Heineken Jazzaldia and the Musical Fortnight, and offers guided tours of the building for visitors.
quote: The venue hosts diverse events including: Cultural performances (Kursaal Eszena), Jazz festival (Jazzaldia), Musical Fortnight, Congresses and meetings. Guided tours are also available as a service for visitors.

claim: Pukas Surf Eskola operates from Avenida de la Zurriola 24 in San Sebastián, teaches surf since 1982 and offers individual, couple, three-person and group lesson formats year-round with booking via their online system.
quote: Pukas Surf Eskola San Sebastián. Avenida de la Zurriola 24. +34 943 320 068. With experience in surf classes since 1982.

claim: A 3-day course (4.5 hours total, 1.5h per session) at Pukas Surf Eskola on Zurriola Beach cost €161 per person including boards and summer wetsuits, working out to roughly €36 per 1.5-hour session.
quote: Cost: €161 per person for a 3-day course (1.5 hours per day = 4.5 hours total)... Surfboards and summer wetsuits provided.

claim: La Perla Thalassotherapy day tickets range €25–€54 with access to marine route, swimming pools, jacuzzis, saunas and aquatic gymnasium; weekday afternoon (13:30–16:00) discounted to €28 and a May–June Sunday Duo promo is €56 for two.
quote: Every Day Access: €25.00 – €54.00... Monday to Friday Afternoon Special (13:30–16:00): €28.00... Duo Promotion (May–June Sundays): €56.00

claim: La Perla is housed in the iconic centre on La Concha beach offering thalassotherapy circuits combining heated seawater pools, jets and saunas next to the bay.
quote: La Perla Thalassotherapy Centre • Spa, Beauty, Sport and Health

claim: Motoras de la Isla runs the Red Line to Santa Clara Island at €5 round trip (every 30 minutes, 10:00–20:00) and the Blue Line bay tour at €8; children under 4 free; high season is 1 June–30 September plus Easter and bank holidays.
quote: Red Line: Standard €5 per person... Blue Line (Bay Tour + Island): Standard €8... High Season: June 1 - September 30, plus Easter and Bank Holidays

claim: AloKayak rents from the harbour ramp next to the Aquarium (Paseo del Muelle 35): single kayak/SUP €14/hour, double €22/hour, family kayak (2 adults + 2 kids) €28/hour, all including paddle, life jacket and dry bag; Santa Clara Island is 800m away, about 20 minutes paddling.
quote: Single Kayak/SUP: €14/hour... Double Kayak/SUP: €22/hour... Family Kayak: €28/hour... 800 metres from our location... in about 20 minutes

claim: Sea water at San Sebastián averages 16°C in May (range 13.5–20.9°C), warming from ~16–17°C early in the month to ~18–19°C by late May — wetsuits still recommended.
quote: Average water temperature in San Sebastian in May is 16°C... Minimum: 13.5°C, Maximum: 20.9°C... temperatures rising from around 16-17°C in early May to approximately 18-19°C by late May.

claim: The official Zurriola swimming season runs June to September with water generally not dropping below 20°C, suitable for comfortable swimming.
quote: The swimming season in Zurriola Beach lasts from June to September, during which the water temperature does not drop below 20°C and is suitable for comfortable swimming.

claim: The Talaia route's Pasaia–Donostia segment is a shorter dramatic coastal section with vertical cliffs, the Lighthouse of La Plata, Mount Ulia caves and the 16th-century Monpás ruins, suited for hikers used to mixed-terrain paths.
quote: Pasaia-Donostia: A shorter segment from Pasaia to San Sebastian, characterized by dramatic coastal scenery with vertical cliffs and forest passages... Lighthouse of La Plata... Mount Ulia with distinctive cave formations... Historic ruins of Monpás with 16th-century origins

claim: The Monte Ulia loop from Gros (trailhead at Zemoria Kalea 47) covers 4.2 km, climbs to 234m at Peña del Rey and takes just over an hour, marked with green/white blazes; the GR-121 (red/white) extension reaches Pasaia.
quote: The official loop trail covers 2.6 miles (4.2 Km) with an excursion duration of slightly over one hour... The highest point reaches Peña del Rey at approximately 768 feet (234 meters)... The trailhead begins at Zemoria Street (Kalea) in the Gros neighborhood... house number 47

claim: La Concha bay is calm and shallow, sheltered by Mount Urgull, Mount Igeldo and Santa Clara Island, making it safe for swimmers of all levels with showers, toilets and lockers on site.
quote: La Concha is a very safe bay for swimming... Mount Urgull on one side and Mount Igeldo on the other protect the waters of La Concha... There's an island blocking the swell at La Concha so it is flat and safe.

claim: Santa Clara Island sits about 500m off shore in La Concha bay and has a small beach with bar, terrace, first-aid post and a natural seawater pool reachable by boat, kayak or open-water swim.
quote: Santa Clara Island is a small, picturesque island located in La Concha Bay, just 500 meters from the coastline of San Sebastian, accessible by boat, kayak, or swimming. The island beach offers all kinds of services, from a bar and terrace to a first aid post, and even its own natural swimming pool with sea water.

claim: Txomin Etxaniz winery in Getaria offers 90-minute guided tour and tasting at €22 per person, Monday-Saturday starting 11:00 or 11:30, with anchovies and Getaria white tuna paired to txakoli; booking via web form required with email confirmation.
quote: Price: €22 per person. Schedule: Open Monday to Saturday (excluding public holidays). Visit time: 11:00-11:30 start. Duration: 90 minutes. guided tour and the tasting of different txakoli wines accompanied with anchovies and white tuna from Getaria.

claim: Hiruzta Bodega in Hondarribia runs 50-minute txakoli tours Wednesday to Sunday plus holidays at 12:00 and 13:00, with optional pintxos and food-pairing packages; bookings via reservas@hiruzta.com.
quote: Tours are available from Wednesday to Sunday and public holidays, with a duration of 50 minutes and visiting hours at 12:00 and 13:00.

claim: Gaintza in Getaria offers a 90-minute vineyard walk and tasting of three estate txakolis (Gaintza, Gaintza Roses, Aitako) for €25, Tuesday to Saturday at 11:30, with afternoon garden tastings overlooking the vineyards Tue–Fri.
quote: Tours run Tuesday to Saturday at 11:30 a.m. (except public holidays), with a duration of 90 minutes. The price is 25 euros.

claim: Petritegi in Astigarraga charges €44.50 per person for the standard cider-house menu (chorizo in cider, cod omelette, cod, txuletón, cheese with walnuts/quince); a bottled-cider version without txotx access costs €3 less, and the kids menu is €19.
quote: Standard Cider House Menu: €44.50. choose our menus with a bottle instead of Txotx option. The price is € 3 less than the price corresponding to the menus with txotx. Children's Menu (up to 14): €19.

claim: The 2026 official txotx season runs Friday 16 January to 3 May, after which most sidrerías close or shift to bottle service; in late May visitors should pick year-round houses like Petritegi or Astarbe to still get the full cider-house menu.
quote: The txotx season starts on Friday 16 January and ends on 3 May. Petritegi Cider House is open all year round and serves up a traditional cider house menu all year round. Astarbe Sagardotegia has been making Basque Cider for over 15 generations and serves up a traditional cider house menu all year round.

claim: Sidrería Zelaia (technically Hernani, closer to Astigarraga) opens Jan–May during txotx with chuletón, cod and tortilla in a menu typically €35–45 per person.
quote: Zelaia is open from January to May during txotx season. Prices for the sidrería menu typically range between 35 and 45 euros.

claim: Mercado de La Bretxa, tucked into the Parte Vieja's basement shopping centre, hosts more than forty stalls of fishmongers, butchers, produce, olives and pickles and is open Monday–Saturday 8:00–17:00, closed Sundays.
quote: La Bretxa Market is San Sebastián's most atmospheric place to shop like a local, tucked into the Old Town, where fishmongers call out the day's catch, butchers prep cuts to order. At the basement of La Bretxa shopping centre, there are more than forty retailers.

claim: Mercado San Martín on Calle Urbieta opened in 1884 and is open Monday–Saturday 08:00–20:00; modernised in 2006, it combines fresh fish, cheese, charcuterie and gourmet stalls with sit-down dining inside the market.
quote: The market is open Monday to Saturday, from 8:00 to 20:00. The market opened in 1884 and was named after the nearby Church of San Martín. It underwent a major renovation in 2006.

claim: Mimo San Sebastián, based in the Hotel María Cristina building, runs hands-on Basque cooking classes from roughly €130 for a 3-hour session up to €230 for the full 5-hour traditional class, with optional market tour and lunch with wines.
quote: Mimo offers a 2.5-hour class starting at 150€ with a special new class offer, and they also have a 3-hour class priced at 130€. For longer experiences, the traditional 5-hour cooking class is priced at 230€.

claim: Kookin Donosti (a smaller alternative to Mimo) bundles a guided market tour with a hands-on Basque class — students typically cook tortilla de patatas, bacalao al pil-pil, txuleta and Basque cheesecake, paired with txakoli, cider or red wine.
quote: Carlos takes you through the market and introduces you to local producers he's built relationships with. Classes typically include a market visit plus cooking class plus lunch with wines, and teach dishes like tortilla de patatas, bacalao al pil-pil, txuleta, and Basque-style cheesecake.

claim: Panadería Galparsoro on Calle Mayor 6 in the Old Town bakes additive-free, no-added-yeast, organic French-style breads, baguettes, walnut-chocolate pastries and croissants; open 8:00–14:00 and 16:30–20:00 with frequent queues.
quote: Calle Mayor, 6, 20003 Donostia / San Sebastián. open 8:00 AM - 2:00 PM, 4:30 PM - 8:00 PM. state of the art breads distinguished by their wheat, made with no additives, no added yeast, all-organic ingredients, and in the traditional French style.

claim: Casa Otaegui, founded 1886 and now run by the fourth and fifth generation, is San Sebastián's oldest pastry shop and the home of the trademarked Panchineta® — a puff-pastry, custard and toasted-almond cake that sells over 1,000 units on busy weekends from the flagship Calle Narrika store in the Parte Vieja.
quote: Casa Otaegui is the oldest pastry shop in Donostia, with over 130 years of uninterrupted artisan work. The authentic Panchineta®, created by Emiliana Malcorra, is a cake that combines crunchy puff pastry, soft custard, and toasted almonds. On the busiest weekends, Casa Otaegui can sell more than 1,000 panchinetas.

claim: The gilda — a skewer of pickled Ibarra guindilla peppers, Manzanilla olives and a Cantabrian anchovy — was invented in 1946 at Bar Casa Vallés on Calle Fermín Calbetón and named after Rita Hayworth's film, characterised as 'verde, picante y salado'.
quote: In 1946, at Bar Casa Vallés on Fermín Calbetón Street in San Sebastián, the bar manager, Joaquín Aranburu, began serving pickled Ibarra guindilla peppers with olives and Cantabrian anchovies on a skewer. both were verde (green), picante (spicy) and salado (salty).

claim: Top stops for the gilda txikiteo circuit include Casa Vallés (the 1942 original), Bar La Cepa de Bernardo, Antonio Bar (a Centro standard with two olives, extra peppers and even two anchovies), Bar Txepetxa and Borda Berri.
quote: Casa Vallés, a frozen-in-time bar founded in 1942 in the city center, is the original birthplace of the gilda. Antonio Bar in the Centro neighborhood comes in clutch with another perfectly-balanced Gilda with two olives, extra peppers, and even two anchovies.

claim: Bar La Viña at 31 de Agosto 3 in the Parte Vieja is the original home of the burnt Basque cheesecake — created by Santiago Rivera around 1988–1990 — sold by the slice for €6 with long queues forming shortly after opening.
quote: A cheesecake slice at La Viña costs €6. There will already be a line in a few minutes after opening.

claim: Santiago Rivera, son of La Viña's 1959 founders, is preparing to hand the bar to the next generation, but his original burnt-cheesecake recipe — smooth and soft inside, dark caramelised crust — is still served by the slice on Calle 31 de Agosto.
quote: Santiago Rivera is widely credited with creating Basque burnt cheesecake at the family-run pintxo bar around 1988 to 1990. Santiago Rivera is preparing to hand La Viña to the next generation.

claim: Gelatería Boulevard on Alameda del Boulevard 20 (with a second branch in Gros near Zurriola beach) is the city's standout ice-cream stop, with generous scoops, 15+ vegan flavours and signature options like pistachio, Ferrero, tiramisu and dark chocolate.
quote: Gelatería Boulevard is known for its huge selection of ice cream flavors, including over 15 vegan options. The main location is at 20 Boulevard Zumardia, Donostia, San Sebastian.

claim: Heladería Arnoldo, in business since 1935, is widely cited as San Sebastián's best traditional ice-cream parlour and an alternative to the Boulevard branch for a Concha or Parte Vieja stroll.
quote: Arnoldo Heladeria, in business since 1935, makes San Sebastián's best ice cream.

claim: The Geoparkea Flysch boat tour departs from Quay Txomin Agirre in Zumaia, lasts 3 hours, and costs €28 adult / €17 under-12.
quote: 28.00 € (Under 12 years: 17.00 €) ... 03:00 ... Quay Txomin Agirre, Zumaia

claim: The boat trip runs from Zumaia past Deba to Mutriku, giving about 45 minutes of free time ashore in Mutriku's historic port.
quote: discover the Geopark coastline from a geological and a cultural point of view ... ship building in Zumaia, trade in Deba and whaling in Mutriku ... The boat trip is dependent on the weather and sea conditions.

claim: The Basque Coast Geopark also offers guided cliff walks and a 'Route of the viewpoints' alongside the boat trip, run from visitor centres in Mutriku, Deba and Zumaia.
quote: The flysch, the ports and maritime tradition by boat ... A sea crossing past the cliffs of the flysch ... Route of the viewpoints

claim: The Basque Coast Geopark has held UNESCO Global Geopark status since 2015 and exposes more than 60 million years of geological history along the Zumaia–Deba–Mutriku coast.
quote: impressive Flysch cliffs from the sea that represent more than 60 million years of geological history

claim: Itzurun beach in Zumaia stood in for Dragonstone in Game of Thrones, and the cliff-top 16th-century San Telmo chapel was built to protect the town's sailors.
quote: Itzurun Beach, famously featured in Game of Thrones, is where Daenerys Targaryen's dramatic return to Dragonstone was filmed ... The small white picturesque chapel perched on the edge of the cliffs directly above Itzurun Beach is the Church of San Telmo

claim: The Dragonstone landing scene was shot at Itzurun in Season 7 Episode 1 'Dragonstone', a roughly one-hour drive from Bilbao.
quote: Itzurun Beach near Bilbao, Spain, located in Zumaia in the Basque Country, was chosen to depict the landing beach at Dragonstone, accessible within an hour's drive from Bilbao

claim: Zarautz, the Basque Country's surf capital, is a 30-minute Euskotren ride from Donostia's Amara station and trains run every 15 minutes (every 30 on Saturdays) for €2.75 each way.
quote: It leaves every 15 minutes (every 30 mins on Saturdays) from the main Euskotren station in Amara ... €2.75 each way ... the Euskotren drops you off pretty much in the centre of Zarautz

claim: Pesa runs hourly buses from Bilbao Airport directly to San Sebastián's northern bus/train station for €17.10 single, taking 75 minutes, with departures every hour from 07:45 to 23:45.
quote: There is one departure per hour from 07:45 to 23:45 ... €17.10 for a single ticket ... 75 minutes to downtown area

claim: The E21 from EAS airport runs every 45–60 minutes, costs €2.75 one-way and reaches Plaza Gipuzkoa in 35–50 minutes; a taxi runs €40–€60 and about 25 minutes.
quote: €2.75 for a one-way ticket ... Bus every 45 mins to 60 mins depending on the time you arrive ... Cost: €40–€60 depending on your hotel location

claim: A cash single on Dbus is €1.95 with no free transfers, but a Mugi card drops the per-trip fare to €0.78 (transferable) or €0.59 (personalised) and includes free interchange between Dbus and Lurraldebus.
quote: Standard fare: €1.95 ... Cash payment of the tickets doesn´t allow free transfers ... Transferable Mugi Card: Day ticket: €0.78 ... 1-20 trips/month: €0.59 per trip

claim: The anonymous transferable Mugi 'Travelcard' costs €5 and is sold without paperwork at newsagents and tobacconists across Gipuzkoa.
quote: It costs €5 and can be purchased from authorised sale points in the application & top-up network (no forms need to be filled in)

claim: Mugi cards are sold at authorised shops displaying the Mugi logo and the same card can be topped up and re-used across Gipuzkoa transport operators.
quote: All Mugi cards can be obtained at authorised establishments (newsagents, book shops and tobacconists) displaying the Mugi symbol
